item.text: Historians distinguish them because they were created under different conditions. A contemporary diary may preserve immediate perceptions, details, and uncertainty, but can still be biased, incomplete, or shaped by private self-presentation. A memoir benefits from hindsight and may explain longer-term significance, yet memory can fade, reorganize events, and reflect later beliefs or motives. Neither is accepted uncritically; historians compare each with other evidence, authorship, audience, and context.
